about.title: Bellflower Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Ten people died in traffic collisions in Bellflower during 2025, according to public records. Each of those numbers was somebody's parent, partner, or child, and behind each one is a household in Los Angeles County trying to figure out what comes next. Wrongful death claims exist for exactly that reason. Under California law, a spouse or domestic partner and children hold the first right to bring a claim; certain dependents and heirs may follow if none of them survive. The claim is civil, meaning it moves on its own track regardless of whether police or prosecutors ever file charges. Families generally have two years from the date of death to act, and that window shrinks when a public agency is involved. Bellflower's roads see steady volume along Clark Avenue, Bellflower Boulevard, Woodruff Avenue and Alondra Boulevard, and collisions here tend to cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on Who May File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children. An attorney in our network can explain where your family fits and who should be named in the claim.

items.title: Deadlines Handled Early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the timeline is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting connected quickly means those dates are tracked from the start.

items.title: Every Category of Loss Considered
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. The attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash on Bellflower Boulevard already led to criminal charges. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, if your family wants to pursue compensation. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, not on repaying your household for what it lost. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action that your family controls, and it can proceed whether or not a conviction ever happens. An attorney can also explain how evidence from the criminal matter may be useful in the civil case.

items.question: My sibling died and had no spouse or children. Can I bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. California gives first priority to a spouse or domestic partner and children, but when none survive, certain dependents and heirs may have standing. Whether you qualify depends on your relationship and, in some cases, on financial dependence. This is one of the first things an attorney will sort out with you.

items.question: What if a city vehicle or a road maintenance issue in Los Angeles County was involved?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity follow a different and much shorter timeline than the usual two years. You typically must file an administrative claim with the agency before any lawsuit can begin. Because those deadlines pass quickly, reaching out to an attorney soon after the death matters even more in these situations.
